title: What this teaching asked of people
intro: TriedPath Fellowship is invented. Its teaching is not: every lesson on this tape comes from a ministry handbook, booklets and a class manual used between 1993 and 1996, and every commercial from a real product, price or flyer of the time. These papers are kept in the Smithsonian's Love in Action Collection. This is what the teaching asked of the people it was written for, in its own words where it can be quoted.

sections.heading: What it asked of the person

items.text: To guard every thought that went in. “It is our responsibility to see that the new information we receive is consistent with our new life.” The handbook's rule for the mind was the computer saying “garbage in/garbage out”.
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, printed p. 130 (PDF p. 138) and p. 131 (PDF p. 139); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: To turn off the radio and the television: “Turn on any radio or television and you will find a mind-boggling barrage of new morality propaganda. … Gays on television are shown as superior people.”
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, printed pp. 130–131 (PDF pp. 138–139); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: To give up their music, their clothes, their bars and their scene. Under “What Do We Lose?” the handbook listed “the associations, triggered by music, clothing and many other things”, and promised that “bars will close, the scene will change”. It called “returning to old haunts” and “reviving the old associations that music brings forth” the way “an ex-gay person stumbles”.
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, printed p. 132 (PDF p. 140) and p. 135 (PDF p. 143); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: To cut off their friends: “Yes, we are the ones who must cut off relationships with those that would keep us in bondage to sin.”
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, printed p. 133 (PDF p. 141); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: To fill the mind until the old life was pushed out: Bible study, prayer and Scripture memorization, “adding mountains of material to your memory tapes. It will be this bulk of the material that ejects the desires and temptations of the old way of life.”
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, printed p. 130 (PDF p. 138) and p. 132 (PDF p. 140); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: To come to every class on time, “lessons read, homework done, pen and binder in hand”, to keep a journal, to take notes at each session, and to spend time each week reflecting on the last session and share it at the next meeting.
items.source: Love in Action, Steps Out Program Class Manual (c. 1994; its latest dated item is June 1994), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 13 Folder 1, Program Overview p. iii (PDF p. 6): “KEEP A JOURNAL!”, “TAKE NOTES at each session”, “Spend time each week reflecting on last week's session. Share at the next meeting”; Group Interaction p. v (PDF p. 16): “Be on time!”, “Come prepared—lessons read, homework done, pen and binder in hand.”; read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: To treat the group as their new family: “Our families were imperfect at best and corrupt at worst. God has given us the opportunity for a new family.” The same page counted on peer pressure: “Peer pressure (group reinforcement) … can play an equally important part in bringing a person out of the gay lifestyle.”
items.source: Love in Action, Steps Out Program Class Manual (c. 1994; its latest dated item is June 1994), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 13 Folder 1, Group Interaction p. i (PDF p. 12); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: If they could, to move away for a year. The handbook called a residential programme “by far, the most effective way”, said that relocating “in itself is often helpful in breaking sinful relationships and patterns”, and asked those who joined to “set aside other life goals” and commit to “a one-year period”, with a “$20.00 non-refundable fee” to receive an application.
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, Chapter Eighteen, “Should You Join a Residential Program?”, printed pp. 176–177 (PDF pp. 184–185); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: To accept that this would be “the most difficult task of your entire life”.
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, printed p. 133 (PDF p. 141); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

sections.heading: Where it told them to look for the cause

items.text: In their families: “We believe that the deepest root of homosexuality is a break in the relational bonds within the family.” Any break in the bond of mother, father and child “will produce insecurity in the child … whether the break is real or only perceived by the child, the results are the same.”
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, printed p. 13 (PDF p. 21); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: In their fathers: “It is when the father abdicates his role that distortions set in.” The 1993 Exodus booklet told the same story of a boy whose father did not “welcome him into the male world”, and who “stays in the kitchen with mom”.
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, printed p. 13 (PDF p. 21); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026; Exodus International–North America, resource booklet #PR-02, Are People Born Gay? (© 1993), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 12, printed pp. 7, 9, 13 (PDF pp. 5, 6, 8) (v4, re-read in the OCR here)

items.text: In their own envy: comparison with other boys becomes admiration, admiration “slips into ENVY”, and “in puberty … envy becomes eroticized”.
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, printed pp. 17–18 (PDF pp. 25–26) (v4)

items.text: Never in their nature. The handbook said “Scientific evidence does not support the theory of constitutional homosexuality”; its own Exodus series printed, in 1996, that people's “claim of not having asked for their orientation is, in most cases, true”, and called it “something they never chose”.
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, printed p. 11 (PDF p. 19) (v4); Exodus International–North America, resource booklet #PR-01, Is Homosexuality Inborn? (© 1996), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 12, printed p. 17 (PDF p. 34) (v4)

items.text: The handbook knew that fighting the thoughts made them stronger: “The more we fight against homosexual thoughts, the more intense they become.” It printed this under the heading “Remember Half The Process Won't Work”.
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, printed p. 133 (PDF p. 141); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: It wrote that “controlling their minds and thoughts is beyond the ability of most people”, and that a slip “brings on a hopelessness, a feeling of failure, that things will never really change”.
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, printed p. 135 (PDF p. 143); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: And it told them the failure was theirs: “If we are ambivalent or even opposed to God's position, the new information will find no permanent home in our minds.” “This places the burden directly on us.”
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, printed p. 133 (PDF p. 141) and p. 130 (PDF p. 138); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

sections.heading: What it asked of pastors, counselors and families

items.text: The handbook was written for them. Its cover reads “A handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”.
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, the cover (PDF p. 2); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: It asked the church to make room for the programme: “the Church has unwittingly overlooked a small, but very significant people group, the ex-gays”, and “generally speaking, the church has not ‘been there’ for the gay person seeking a way out.”
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, Introduction, printed p. 1 (PDF p. 9); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: The Exodus booklet series offered “specialized information for parents, friends, spouses, pastors and counselors”: “special booklets on relating to a gay loved one: whether a son, daughter, spouse, parent, friend, co-worker, or neighbor”, and, for the church, “special helps for pastors”.
items.source: Exodus International–North America, “Resource Booklets” (the back page printed after each booklet in the series), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 12, PDF p. 13, “Resource Booklets” and “Booklet Categories”; read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: It asked women to take part too. A church flyer of June 1992 invited “All Married and Single Women” to a class called “Women Relating to Men”; one of its five topics was “Single women relating to ex-gay men”.
items.source: The flyer “Women Relating to Men … For All Married and Single Women”, Thursday 11 June 1992, 7:30 P.M., Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 1 Folder 3 (“Women Only”), PDF p. 17, the flyer's text; read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

sections.heading: What the commercials are made from

items.text: The Pocket Library is invented. The real Exodus booklets were numbered #PR-01 to #PR-13 (© 1993–1998), and an Exodus booklet was priced 1.00 in 1987.
items.source: Exodus International–North America, “Resource Booklets” (the back page printed after each booklet in the series), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 12, PDF p. 13, the codes on the booklets in the folder; read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026; Emotional Dependency (Exodus International–North America edition, 1987), back cover, priced “1.00”, Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 9, PDF p. 15, the back cover; read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: “Mountains of Material” is invented. Its name is the handbook's own phrase for Scripture memorization: “adding mountains of material to your memory tapes”.
items.source: Love in Action, Helping People Step Out of Homosexuality (“a handbook for pastors, counselors, lay workers”), revised edition © 1995 (first published © 1984 as Steps Out of Homosexuality), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 2 Folder 13, printed p. 130 (PDF p. 138) and p. 132 (PDF p. 140); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: Roots and Recovery was a real video, sold for $20 with “an overview of nine proven principles”. The listing even warned that its “product quality is not typical … However, we make this resource available due to the relevance of its message.” This listing is from 2001, after this tape's year.
items.source: Focus on the Family, the truth comes out: The Roots and Causes of Male Homosexuality (© 2001), resources pages, printed p. 39 (PDF p. 22), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 6 Folder 5, the listing “Understanding Homosexuality: Roots and Recovery”; read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: The Un-Walk Steps class is invented. Its rules are the Love in Action class manual's own: “There is no free lunch!”, “KEEP A JOURNAL!”, “Be on time!”, “lessons read, homework done, pen and binder in hand”.
items.source: Love in Action, Steps Out Program Class Manual (c. 1994; its latest dated item is June 1994), Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 13 Folder 1, Program Overview p. iii (PDF p. 6); Group Interaction p. v (PDF p. 16); read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: Women Relating to Men is a real flyer: its title, its two hooks (“I Don't Want To Go To This Class!”, “I Wish I Had Gone To This Class”) and its five topics. Its presenters and its church are not named here.
items.source: The flyer “Women Relating to Men … For All Married and Single Women”, Thursday 11 June 1992, 7:30 P.M., Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428 (the Mattachine Society of Washington “Love in Action” Collection), Box 1 Folder 3 (“Women Only”), PDF p. 17, the flyer's text; read on the page image, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: In December 1973 the American Psychiatric Association's Board of Trustees voted to remove homosexuality from its diagnostic manual.
items.source: Jack Drescher, “Out of DSM: Depathologizing Homosexuality”, Behavioral Sciences 5(4):565–575, 2015 (PMC4695779), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4695779/ read 15 Nov 2026

items.text: In 1987 the last trace, “ego-dystonic homosexuality”, was removed in the manual's revision, DSM-III-R.
items.source: Jack Drescher, “Out of DSM: Depathologizing Homosexuality”, Behavioral Sciences 5(4):565–575, 2015 (PMC4695779), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4695779/ read 15 Nov 2026

items.text: In May 1990 the World Health Organization adopted ICD-10, whose note reads: “Sexual orientation by itself is not to be regarded as a disorder.”
items.source: World Health Organization, ICD-10 (browser, 2019 version), block F66, Note, https://icd.who.int/browse10/2019/en/GetConcept?ConceptId=F66 read 15 Nov 2026; adoption “May 1990 (WHA43.24)”, https://www.who.int/standards/classifications/classification-of-diseases read 15 Nov 2026
